author: cskiraly
content:
<@363800010518822915> <@412614104222531604> <@1257246783503994940>  my version is now pushed at https://github.com/cskiraly/prysm/tree/seacast-devnet-clean

Things to know:
- definitely not production quality, it didn't try to be
- it implements a subset of the SEACAST spec. The spec is executable Python: a small simulator runs its code as written (I hope I don't have to expand on the advantages of that).
- most of SEACAST also has a Lean 4 transcription, function by function, checked against the Python by replaying the simulator's traces. That has its own advantages towards proven properties.
- part of SEACAST also has some FV: proofs in Veil of models of its rules. Small parts, so don't take it as anything else than a step in that direction.
- why a subset? Because SEACAST was built to cover several use cases in a coherent way. That might look like a disadvantage if you look at the amount of spec lines. But a specific use, such as this, uses much less, a subset. My implementation is a research implementation, so its code has more than the subset needs (options this branch leaves off, fault injections for tests). Don't judge the subset's size by it.
- this exact version hasn't run on a devnet yet: the devnet runs so far used an earlier version of the same code. This one is now being double-checked ...
